title: Convert Sorted Array to Binary Search Tree
statement_short: Given an integer array nums where the elements are sorted in ascending order, convert it to a height-balanced binary search tree. A height-balanced tree is one in which the depth of the two subtrees of every node never differs by more than 1.
constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 10^4, -10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4, nums is sorted in strictly increasing order
hint: Sorted array with length up to 10^4 allows recursively picking the middle element as root to build subtrees.
why_not: Right: Tree DFS recursively picks middle array elements as roots and constructs left/right subtrees in O(n) time and O(log n) space. Not Binary Search: Binary search locates target values in arrays, but building a BST structure uses recursive divide-and-conquer DFS. Not Two Pointers: Array pointers define subsegment bounds, but the tree construction backbone is recursive DFS. Not Tree BFS: Level-order building using queues requires complex index range tracking compared to top-down DFS.
